title: calm-type — a step-by-step type-inference visualizer for teaching Hindley-Milner
summary: A from-scratch offline web application implementing a small ML-like language whose unification engine visualizes every inference step, constraint, and substitution as students type.

title: coldstash — a crypto-shredding cold-storage engine with per-tenant deletion proofs
summary: A from-scratch Python storage engine that writes immutable, per-tenant-keyed chunks to cold object storage and makes deletion a verifiable act of key destruction rather than an unlink promise.

title: fragment-trace — no_std heap-fragmentation profiler for bare-metal Rust
summary: A from-scratch no_std instrumentation library that records every allocator event on Cortex-M MCUs into a lock-free SRAM ring buffer and reconstructs a fragmentation timeline on the host.

title: quorum-mesh — store-carry-forward gossip daemon for off-internet neighborhoods
summary: A from-scratch Elixir daemon that carries signed, encrypted message bundles between phones and Linux routers over BLE and Wi-Fi Direct, syncing a delay-tolerant local web when the internet is unavailable or censored.

title: speak-diff — a narrating CLI that makes code review audible for blind developers
summary: A from-scratch C# command-line tool that parses unified diffs into semantic units and narrates them through the OS speech pipeline with review-specific pacing, voice earcons, and structural cues.

title: apprentice-log — offline competency evidence for vocational apprentices
summary: A from-scratch Swift mobile app that lets apprentices capture signed competency evidence in connectivity-poor workshops and export a verifiable mastery portfolio without any cloud account or monthly fee.

title: attention-ledger — double-entry focus accounting for personal knowledge work
summary: A from-scratch Go desktop app that journals every window-focus change into a local append-only ledger and reconciles declared work intents against actual attention, producing weekly balance sheets of where focus really went.

title: buzzline — a haptic presence vocabulary for small teams over direct BLE
summary: A from-scratch Swift SDK and wearable app that encodes short teammate-presence nudges into a shared haptic vocabulary exchanged phone-to-phone over BLE, with no cloud relay, no message log, and no location data.

title: carbon-cruise — a kernel governor that schedules laptop work by grid carbon intensity
summary: A from-scratch Linux cpufreq kernel module that shifts deferrable local work such as builds and backups into low-carbon electricity windows, exposing carbon budgets as a first-class per-process-group scheduling policy.

title: delta-room — a federated decision log that diffs what a team agreed from what happened
summary: A from-scratch Kotlin server, shipped as a self-hosted container image, that turns every team decision into a signed delta in an append-only room log and federates rooms between instances with an obligation-diff view.

title: drill-forge — a spaced-repetition engine whose cards are typed programs, not static text
summary: A from-scratch TypeScript study framework where every flashcard is a small parameterized expression evaluated fresh at review time, paired with a de-novo decay scheduler and CRDT deck sync across offline-capable devices.

title: envdock — a machine-checked specification for reproducible development environments
summary: A from-scratch Python toolchain that declares a team's pinned development environment in one manifest and conformance-checks any laptop or CI runner against it, emitting machine-readable drift reports for fleets.

title: kadence — a compiler that type-checks your workday before you live it
summary: A from-scratch OCaml TUI that compiles a day-plan written in a small constraint language into a concrete time-blocked schedule, reporting overlaps, starved deep-work, and recovery violations as compile errors with source spans.

title: pair-pulse — blind pairing rotations that cross-pollinate team knowledge
summary: A from-scratch F# serverless API that computes fair rotating pairing schedules for team learning sessions from affinity sketches, so the host can learn pairings without ever holding readable skill data.

title: tone-check — a local linter for escalation patterns in team messages
summary: A from-scratch JavaScript browser extension that lints outgoing team messages for blame framing, passive aggression, and late-night send pressure entirely inside the tab, with zero network permissions and no keystrokes stored.
